key_insight: Laser-assisted friction stir welding joined dissimilar-thickness Al 5052 and DP 590 steel sheets, achieving 193 MPa tensile strength—approximately 88% of the Al base-metal strength.
engineering_relevance: The process offers a promising route to lightweight automotive Al–steel structures while reducing welding axial force relative to conventional friction stir welding.
method: Join 2.5 mm Al 5052 to 1.4 mm DP 590 steel using laser-assisted friction stir welding.
Vary tool rotational and travel speeds to evaluate tensile strength and axial force.
Characterize the joint interface and identify intermetallic phases using X-ray diffraction.
evidence_signal: The study reported a peak tensile strength of 193 MPa, lower axial force than conventional FSW, and an approximately 5 μm interface layer containing FeAl, Fe2Al5, and Fe4Al13.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish fatigue or corrosion performance, which require validation before automotive deployment.
paper_title: Joining of Al 5052 Alloy to Advanced High-Strength Steel Sheets of Dissimilar Thickness Using Laser-Assisted Friction Stir Welding
